faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium ion implantation electrode?

faq.q: How is a titanium ion implantation electrode manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium ion implantation electrode is manufactured using Precision CNC turning; Electropolishing; Class 100 cleanroom cleaning; Helium leak testing. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium ion implantation electrode?
faq.a: Stainless steel (heavier, less fatigue life), aluminum (lower strength)

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium ion implantation electrode?
faq.a: Titanium Ion Implantation Electrode components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348, ASME. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium ion implantation electrode?
faq.a: With proper material selection (Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V) and manufacturing process control (thread rolling, heat treatment), titanium titanium ion implantation electrode components exhibit excellent fatigue life and corrosion resistance in service.
